lens_note: architecture lens stuck >22min over-verifying the gleam_time calendar/timestamp API (which compiles clean); its architectural concerns are covered by blind+edge (transient trade-off) and codebase+acceptance (now_iso boundary, docstrings). Degraded guard (zero findings) does NOT apply — 6 lenses produced actionable findings.

B1.evidence: all 5 guarded-UPDATE Error branches (step_t0 :343, step_co_nudge :396, step_reminder :445, step_warm_handoff :491, step_terminal :553) now call mark_failed(db, sentry, row.id, <specific reason>) + the capture() helper Sentry-captures; mark_failed sets status='failed' (excluded by due-SELECT) so the poison row leaves the queue — the infinite re-send loop is broken. terminal_reason is plain TEXT so the free-form reason string is safe.

W1.evidence: bootstrap() (:169) + sweep_handler (:37) now pass sweep.now_iso() (timestamp.system_time |> to_rfc3339 utc_offset); server compiles clean, so the API resolves.

W2.evidence: step_warm_handoff (:480) passes the real this-tick `outcomes` to dispatch_warm_handoff, which appends outcomes_to_entries(outcomes) (:571-574) instead of the fabricated single email/reminder_2 entry.

W3.evidence: dispatch_warm_handoff now case-matches notify_reference_unreachable's Result (:595-625): Ok->Nil, Error->wisp.log_error + sentry_client.capture(ReferenceWarmHandoffLost). No longer `let _ =`.

W4.evidence: sweep_handler threads sentry_client.Disabled in BOTH SendDeps (:37) and sweep.run (:44) — matches spec OWNS #7.

W5.evidence: cadence_offsets_pinned_with_fake_clock_test (:619-668) seeds 4 rows at a shared anchor, runs the sweep at anchor+1s, asserts offset_seconds == 24/24/48/48h. Sound design; pins the AD-4 increments a step-advance-only test cannot catch.

N2.evidence: mark_failed (:649) now passes the per-call `reason` to sweep_mark_failed (the generic reason_processing_error const was removed) — terminal_reason now carries the specific cause.

new_findings.title: Chosen B1 fix (mark_failed on Error) terminalises healthy rows on a transient UPDATE error — orphaning an already-sent T0 invite
new_findings.evidence:
Error(err) ->
  mark_failed(db, sentry, row.id, "T0 claim failed: " <> query_error(err))
new_findings.detail: r1 endorsed 'mark_failed on Error' as one of two fixes, and B1's silent loop IS broken (row → status='failed' → excluded from due-SELECT, Sentry-captured). BUT a transient per-row error (deadlock/timeout/connection-drop on a healthy row) now permanently fails the row + orphans the invite sent just before the claim. Loud + recoverable, but a one-off DB hiccup can kill a legitimate reference-check.
new_findings.recommended_fix: Either accept with the documented Sentry-loud recovery path, or add a consecutive-error cap (e.g. re-arm for N ticks, terminalise on the Nth) to distinguish poison data from a transient. r1's alternative option.

new_findings.title: B1 Error→mark_failed transition (5 guarded branches) has zero test coverage — the round's primary fix rests on inspection only
new_findings.evidence: grep for mark_failed|'failed'|Failed in the sweep integration test file → no matches. The 5 Error branches now terminalise but no test pins status='failed' on a guarded-UPDATE error.
new_findings.detail: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS (P0 100%, P1 <90%). Hard to test (needs a forced UPDATE error: a CHECK violation or a mock), but the fix is the round's headline change and its new terminalise-on-Error behaviour is unverified beyond reading.
new_findings.recommended_fix: Add a targeted test: seed a row whose guarded UPDATE will error (e.g. a CHECK/trigger violation, or a unit-level mark_failed path test) and assert status='failed' + terminal_reason set. Or pin at least one branch via a mark_failed unit test.

new_findings.title: mark_failed fire-and-forgets its own DB write — newly load-bearing on every error path
new_findings.evidence:
Ok(row_uuid) -> { let _ = sql.sweep_mark_failed(db, row_uuid, reason); Nil }   // Result discarded
capture(sentry, row_id, reason, "processing error")   // runs regardless
Failed
new_findings.detail: Now that mark_failed fires on every guarded Error, a mark_failed write that itself fails leaves the row due (re-selected next tick). capture() always runs (loud), and a global write failure also fails the due-SELECT — so the residual loop only opens in the rare read-ok/write-fail window. Minor residual of B1.
new_findings.recommended_fix: Accept (loud + rare), or log when sweep_mark_failed returns 0 rows so ops can distinguish 'already terminalised by a concurrent writer' from 'write failed'.

new_findings.title: sweep_mark_failed WHERE omits attempt_count — a committed-but-errored advance can be clobbered
new_findings.evidence:
mark_failed: WHERE id = $1 AND status IN ('queued','contact_initiated')   // no attempt_count
advance:   WHERE id = $1 AND status = 'contact_initiated' AND attempt_count = $4
new_findings.detail: If a guarded advance commits but the client sees an error (connection drop between commit + result read), mark_failed runs: status is still 'contact_initiated' (advance doesn't change status) so it matches and wrongly terminalises a successfully-advanced row (+ a reminder already sent). Rare ambiguous-outcome window.
new_findings.recommended_fix: Add attempt_count = $n to sweep_mark_failed's WHERE (the caller knows the expected count), so a row that already advanced is not clobbered.

new_findings.title: sweep_handler module docstring contradicts the W4 fix — claims live Sentry escalation
new_findings.evidence: "Runs against the live config (DB + Resend + Twilio + Sentry), so failures escalate to Sentry the same as a scheduled tick."   // but the fix threads sentry_client.Disabled
new_findings.detail: W4 fixed the handler to thread sentry_client.Disabled (manual runs don't escalate), but the module doc still promises live Sentry escalation. A future reader is misled.
new_findings.recommended_fix: Update the docstring to state manual runs use sentry_client.Disabled (failures are logged, not escalated).

new_findings.title: run/5 docstring still claims 'production passes ""' — W1 fix left it stale
new_findings.evidence: "`now_iso` is an ISO-8601 timestamp string, or "" to let Postgres default to now() (production passes ""; tests pin the clock...)"   // but bootstrap() now passes now_iso()
new_findings.detail: W1 made bootstrap() pass a real now_iso(); the run/5 docstring still says production passes "".
new_findings.recommended_fix: Update the docstring: production passes sweep.now_iso(); "" is the test-pin value.

verdict_rationale: All 6 r1 findings (B1 + W1-W5) are FIXED and verified against the code at 33d237e (N2 incidentally fixed); the load-bearing invariants (exactly-once guarded update, terminal-respect due-SELECT, no-duplicate-T0) are intact — the fix touched only Gleam Error branches + helpers, not the SQL or the due-SELECT. 0 blockers. 2 warnings are the chosen B1 fix's trade-off (transient→terminal, endorsed by r1, loud+recoverable) and a coverage gap on that same fix (hard to test, inspection-thorough); neither blocks. 8 r1 notes carried (advisory, untouched).
